tools.description:
Reads a budget's performance history using the DescribeBudgetPerformanceHistory API:
for each period, the amount budgeted and the actual cost or usage. Use it to answer "was this
budget over last month?" or "which months breached?"; the `budgets` tool covers only the current
period. Read-only.

- Only DAILY, MONTHLY and QUARTERLY budgets have history. A CUSTOM or ANNUALLY budget returns a
  validation_error.
- The tool returns the service's default window: up to 13 MONTHLY periods (this month and the
  previous 12), 4 QUARTERLY periods or 60 DAILY periods. History starts when the budget was
  created (or re-created), whatever its start date, so a newer budget returns fewer periods:
  one created this period returns only the current one.
- `periods` are oldest first. Each has `start` and `end` (UTC dates; the end is exclusive, the
  start of the next period), `budgeted_amount` (the limit that applied in that period; null when
  the budget had none for it) and `actual_amount` (null when no actual data is available). The
  last period is the one containing today, so its actual amount is to date, not final.
- Amounts are decimal strings with a `unit`: compare them as numbers. For RI and Savings Plans
  utilization and coverage budgets they are percentages, and a period breached when
  `actual_amount` is below `budgeted_amount`; for COST and USAGE budgets, when it is above.
- `actual_amount` is measured with the budget's own filter and cost settings, so it can differ
  from an unfiltered Cost Explorer total.
- `time_unit` is often null: the service omits it for many budgets, and nothing in a budget's
  definition shows which. Take the time unit from the `budgets` tool, which always returns it.
- An unknown `budget_name` (an exact name) returns NotFoundException.

Pagination: the whole history fits in one page (at most 60 periods), so omit `max_items`;
passing it only trims the result, and `next_token` continues a trimmed one.

The account ID is retrieved automatically or you may pass `account_id`.

account_id.description: Optional AWS account ID; retrieved automatically if not provided.

max_items.description: Optional total number of periods to return. Omit it to fetch every page.

next_token.description: Optional pagination token from a previous response.

tools.title: Budget Performance History

tools.description:
Retrieves AWS cost anomalies using the Cost Explorer GetAnomalies API.

This tool allows you to retrieve cost anomalies detected on your AWS account during a specified time period.
Anomalies are available for up to 90 days.

Date range matching: an anomaly is returned when its end_date (the last day it was detected) falls
within start_date..end_date. Its start_date can be earlier than the requested start_date: an
anomaly that began before the range and was still being detected inside it is in range. When asked
for anomalies in a period (for example "the past 7 days"), report every returned anomaly, and do
not drop results whose start_date is before the range.

You can filter anomalies by:
- Date range (required)
- Monitor ARN (optional)
- Feedback status (optional)
- Total impact (optional): total_impact_start alone matches total impact >= that value;
  with total_impact_end it matches start..end inclusive. total_impact_operator overrides
  this and compares against total_impact_start; total_impact_end is used only with BETWEEN.

Note: Both start_date and end_date are INCLUSIVE. To get anomalies including today, use today's date as end_date.

Date window: GetAnomalies serves only today minus 90 days through today (UTC); anomalies that
ended earlier cannot be retrieved. A start_date before that, or an end_date after today, is
limited to the window, and data.time_range shows the dates used: when limited_from_request is
true, report the period from time_range.start_date to time_range.end_date, not the requested
one. A range with no day inside the window returns a validation_error that states the window.
With next_token, pass the same start_date and end_date as the first call.

Feedback status options:
- YES: Anomalies marked as accurate
- NO: Anomalies marked as inaccurate
- PLANNED_ACTIVITY: Anomalies marked as planned activities

Pagination:
- max_items: total number of anomalies returned. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result.
  Pass it, or narrow the filters (monitor_arn, total impact, a shorter date range), for
  accounts with many anomalies.
- Anomalies come back newest first (by anomaly end date), so max_items=N returns the N most
  recent.
- If the result has complete_dataset: false, it is partial: call again with a larger
  max_items, continue with next_token, or say the result is partial.

Results:
- impact.total_impact is in dollars: actual spend minus expected spend over the anomaly
  (total_actual_spend - total_expected_spend), not a percentage; total_impact_percentage is
  the percentage. The total impact filter compares against this value. BETWEEN includes both
  bounds. Every comparison uses the unrounded value (responses round it to cents), so EQUAL
  rarely matches.
- A monitor_arn in this account that matches no monitor returns an empty list, not an error.

start_date.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (inclusive). Required.

end_date.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (inclusive — use today's date to include today's anomalies). Required.

monitor_arn.description: Optional ARN of a specific cost anomaly monitor to filter results.

feedback.description: Optional filter for anomalies by feedback status (YES, NO, PLANNED_ACTIVITY).

max_items.description: Optional total number of anomalies to return. None fetches every page.

next_token.description: Optional pagination token from a previous response.

total_impact_operator.description: Optional numeric operator for filtering by total impact (EQUAL, GREATER_THAN, LESS_THAN, GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL, LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL, BETWEEN). Needs total_impact_start. Defaults to GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL when only total_impact_start is given, BETWEEN when total_impact_end is also given.

total_impact_start.description: Optional dollar value the operator compares against (the lower bound for BETWEEN).

total_impact_end.description: Optional upper bound in dollars, inclusive. Used only with BETWEEN; needs total_impact_start.

tools.description:
Lists the Cost Anomaly Detection monitors and alert subscriptions defined in the account,
using the Cost Explorer GetAnomalyMonitors and GetAnomalySubscriptions APIs. Use it to see what
the monitor behind an anomaly tracks and who is alerted; use cost-anomaly for the anomalies.
This tool is read-only.

operation (required): list_monitors or list_subscriptions; any other value is a validation_error.
1. list_monitors: returns data.monitors.
   - monitor_type DIMENSIONAL tracks each value of monitor_dimension (SERVICE, LINKED_ACCOUNT,
     TAG or COST_CATEGORY) separately, and dimensional_value_count is how many values it tracks.
     An anomaly's dimension_value from such a monitor is one of those values: a service name for
     SERVICE, an account ID for LINKED_ACCOUNT. For TAG and COST_CATEGORY, monitor_specification
     names the tag or cost category key.
   - monitor_type CUSTOM tracks the costs that monitor_specification (a Cost Explorer filter
     expression) selects; monitor_dimension is null.
2. list_subscriptions: returns data.subscriptions.
   - A subscription alerts its subscribers about anomalies from the monitors in
     monitor_arn_list whose impact meets threshold_expression. Its dimensions are
     ANOMALY_TOTAL_IMPACT_ABSOLUTE (USD) and ANOMALY_TOTAL_IMPACT_PERCENTAGE (percent); And
     requires every condition, Or any. threshold is a deprecated absolute-USD field and can be
     null: read threshold_expression.
   - frequency DAILY or WEEKLY sends an email digest; IMMEDIATE sends to an SNS topic.
     subscribers holds email addresses or SNS topic ARNs; status DECLINED means the subscriber has
     declined (unsubscribed from) the alerts.
   - Subscriptions decide who is alerted, not what is detected: cost-anomaly also returns
     anomalies below every threshold.
   - An empty monitor_arn_list means the subscription is attached to no monitor, so it sends
     no alerts.

monitor_arn (optional): list_monitors returns only that monitor; list_subscriptions returns
only the subscriptions attached to it. On either operation, a monitor ARN in this account that
matches no monitor returns an empty list, not an error; a malformed ARN is a ValidationException
and another account's ARN is an AccessDeniedException.

Pagination:
- max_items: total monitors or subscriptions returned. Omit it to fetch every page.
- If the result has complete_dataset: false, it is partial: call again with a larger
  max_items, continue with next_token, or say the result is partial.

monitor_arn.description:
Optional monitor ARN. list_monitors returns only that monitor;
list_subscriptions returns only the subscriptions attached to it.

max_items.description: Optional total number of items to return. None fetches every page.

next_token.description: Optional pagination token from a previous response.

tools.description:
Retrieves AWS cost comparisons between two one-month periods.

Do not use this tool except for comparing the costs of one month to the costs of another month. This tool should not be used for week-over-week or quarter-over-quarter (e.g., comparing Q2 vs. Q1) analysis.

USE THIS TOOL ONLY FOR:
- **Month-to-month cost variance analysis** (e.g., January vs February)
- **Root cause analysis** of cost changes between specific months
- **Detailed cost driver identification** (what exactly caused the cost change)
- **Service-level impact analysis** for month-over-month changes
- **Executive reporting** on monthly cost variances

STRICT LIMITATIONS (requests that break them fail with validation_error and no AWS call):
- ONLY compares exactly one month to another month
- Both periods must start on 1st day of month, end on 1st day of next month
- The two periods must be different months (either one may be the earlier)
- Only completed months: the current month and future months are rejected
- Cannot compare weeks, quarters, or custom periods: use cost-explorer getCostAndUsage
- DO NOT USE for general cost analysis or flexible time periods

This tool supports two main operations:
1. getCostAndUsageComparisons: Compare costs between two time periods with flexible grouping and filtering
2. getCostComparisonDrivers: Identify key factors driving cost changes between two time periods

Both operations require:
- BaselineTimePeriod: The reference period, usually the earlier one (must be exactly one month)
- ComparisonTimePeriod: The period compared against the baseline, usually the later one (must be exactly one month)
- MetricForComparison: The cost metric to compare (e.g., BlendedCost, UnblendedCost)

Supported metrics (exact case):
- AmortizedCost: Costs with upfront and recurring reservation fees spread across the period
- BlendedCost: Average cost of all usage throughout the billing period
- NetAmortizedCost: Amortized cost after discounts
- NetUnblendedCost: Unblended cost after discounts
- NormalizedUsageAmount: Normalized usage amount. getCostAndUsageComparisons only
- UnblendedCost: Actual costs incurred during the specified period
- UsageQuantity: Usage amounts in their respective units. getCostAndUsageComparisons only
getCostComparisonDrivers accepts only the five cost metrics.

You can group results by dimensions such as:
- SERVICE: AWS service (e.g., Amazon EC2, Amazon S3)
- LINKED_ACCOUNT: Member accounts in an organization
- REGION: AWS Region
- USAGE_TYPE: Type of usage (e.g., BoxUsage:t2.micro)
- INSTANCE_TYPE: EC2 instance type (e.g., t2.micro, m5.large)
- PLATFORM: Operating system (e.g., Linux/UNIX, Windows (Amazon VPC))
- TENANCY: Instance tenancy. Exact, case-sensitive values: Shared, Dedicated, Host
- RECORD_TYPE: Record type (e.g., Usage, Credit, Tax)
- LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME: AWS seller of record

Costs with no value for a grouped dimension come back under a placeholder such as NoRegion or
NoTenancy, including in each comparison's cost_and_usage_selector. The placeholder is not a
value: a filter on it matches nothing. To filter on those costs, pass the empty string:
`{"Dimensions": {"Key": "REGION", "Values": [""]}}`.

Note:
- Time periods must start and end on the first day of a month, with a duration of exactly one month
- The getCostComparisonDrivers operation automatically includes SERVICE and USAGE_TYPE dimensions
- Data is available for the last 13 months, or up to 38 months if multi-year data is enabled.
  A period starting more than 38 months ago is rejected locally. For 14-38 months back,
  Cost Explorer decides; if it reports the data unavailable, the error carries a hint
  about multi-year data

Filter (optional): a Cost Explorer Expression using And, Or, Not, Dimensions, Tags or
CostCategories. Keys and values match exactly, including case: get them from cost-explorer
getDimensionValues (or getTagsOrValues, getCostCategories). Rejected with validation_error and no
AWS call:
- MatchOptions other than EQUALS and CASE_SENSITIVE (the default), plus ABSENT for Tags and
  CostCategories. The comparison APIs ignore the others (CASE_INSENSITIVE, STARTS_WITH,
  ENDS_WITH, CONTAINS, ...) and still match exactly, so a value in another case or a partial
  value would silently return $0 or no drivers (or everything under Not)
- ABSENT together with Values: the comparison APIs drop the Values
- A RESOURCE_ID filter
- Nesting of 97 or more And/Or/Not levels, which fails in Cost Explorer
In group_by, Cost Explorer itself rejects RESOURCE_ID and USAGE_TYPE_GROUP.

Pagination (both operations):
- max_items: total number of comparisons or drivers returned. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result. Pass it, or narrow group_by/filter, for comparisons that can be large (for
  example grouped by USAGE_TYPE or LINKED_ACCOUNT).
- If the result has complete_dataset: false, it is partial: call again with a larger
  max_items, continue with next_token, or say the result is partial.
- total_cost_and_usage comes from the first page only and isn't repeated on continuation
  calls.

baseline_start_date.description: Baseline period start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (must be first day of month)

baseline_end_date.description: Baseline period end date in YYYY-MM-DD format (must be first day of next month)

comparison_start_date.description: Comparison period start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (must be first day of month)

comparison_end_date.description: Comparison period end date in YYYY-MM-DD format (must be first day of next month)

metric_for_comparison.description: The metric to compare, exact case. getCostAndUsageComparisons: AmortizedCost, BlendedCost, NetAmortizedCost, NetUnblendedCost, NormalizedUsageAmount, UnblendedCost, UsageQuantity. getCostComparisonDrivers: the five *Cost metrics only

group_by.description: Optional grouping of results as a JSON string (e.g., '[{"Type": "DIMENSION", "Key": "SERVICE"}]')

filter.description: Optional Cost Explorer Expression as a JSON string. Keys and values match exactly, including case; MatchOptions only EQUALS/CASE_SENSITIVE (plus ABSENT, without Values, for Tags and CostCategories); no RESOURCE_ID

max_items.description: Total comparisons or drivers to return. None fetches every page.

next_token.description: Pagination token from a previous response

billing_view_arn.description: Optional ARN of a specific billing view

tools.description:
Retrieves AWS Free Tier usage information using the Free Tier Usage API.

This tool provides insights into your AWS Free Tier usage across services:

1. get_free_tier_usage: Shows your current Free Tier usage across AWS services
   - Helps identify where you are approaching Free Tier limits
   - Shows actual usage against Free Tier allocations
   - Returns `data.freeTierUsages`, a `data.summary` computed over the returned rows, and `data.pagination`

SUMMARY (`data.summary`):
- Each row is counted as at_limit (99.9% or more of its limit), near_limit (80% to under 99.9%), safe (under 80%) or unknown (no usable limit or usage), by actual month-to-date usage. Items are listed for at_limit and near_limit, highest first.
- forecast_exceeds_limit_items lists rows still under the limit whose month-end forecast (forecastedUsageAmount) reaches 99.9% or more of it, highest first. The forecast is month-to-date usage projected in a straight line to month end, so early in the month it can greatly overstate. Rows already at the limit are not repeated there.
- Each item is one row, with its `forecast`, `region` and `free_tier_type`, and `forecast_percentage` when the forecast is at least the actual usage (the API defaults the forecast to 0, and a forecast below actual usage is not a real one). One service can have a row per region, so read `region` before saying which limit is reached. free_tier_type tells whether the offer ends ("12 Months Free", "Free Trial") or does not ("Always Free"); an empty one says neither.

FILTER (optional JSON string):
- Shape: {"Dimensions": {"Key": "SERVICE", "Values": ["AmazonSNS"], "MatchOptions": ["EQUALS"]}}. MatchOptions is required and takes exactly one option. A row matches if it matches any of the Values.
- Combine filters with {"And": [...]} or {"Or": [...]} (at least 2 filters each) or {"Not": {...}}. Each object holds exactly one of Dimensions, And, Or, Not.
- Keys SERVICE, OPERATION, USAGE_TYPE, REGION, FREE_TIER_TYPE and DESCRIPTION take EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH or CONTAINS. Matching ignores case and spaces, so "awslambda" matches "AWS Lambda".
- Each value is at most 20 characters of letters, digits, spaces and - : . _ / , $ ( ). A long service name such as "Amazon Simple Notification Service" is rejected. Use CONTAINS with part of the name ("Notification"), or the short code the API accepts for some long names (AmazonSNS, AmazonEC2, AmazonS3, AmazonRDS, AmazonSES, AWSSQS).
- REGION is a region code such as us-east-1, or "global".
- FREE_TIER_TYPE is one of "Always Free", "12 Months Free" or "Free Trial" (empty for a row with no type).
- USAGE_PERCENTAGE is actual usage as a percent of the limit. It takes GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL and one number from 0 to 100 (80 means 80%). Only USAGE_PERCENTAGE takes GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL.

PAGINATION:
- max_items: total usage rows returned. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result. Pass it, or narrow the filter, when the account has many Free Tier rows.
- A partial result has `complete_dataset: false` and a warning. The summary then covers only the returned rows, so its counts undercount. Call again with a larger max_items, continue with next_token (the `pagination.next_token` from that response, sent with the same filter), or state in the answer that the result is partial.
- A continuation call's summary covers only that call's rows.

filter.description: Optional filter as a JSON string, in the shape the description gives.

max_items.description: Total usage rows to return. None fetches every page.

next_token.description: Continuation token from a previous response.

tools.description:
Get detailed cost optimization recommendation with integrated data from multiple AWS services.

This tool combines data from:
- Cost Optimization Hub (base recommendation)
- AWS Compute Optimizer (detailed metrics for compute resources)
- Cost Explorer (Savings Plans/RI purchase recommendations)

It provides comprehensive analysis with utilization metrics, savings calculations, and implementation guidance.

COMMITMENT PURCHASE DETAILS:
- For PurchaseReservedInstances, additional_details is the Cost Explorer reservation purchase
  recommendation for the recommendation's service, term and payment option. It may list several
  instance types and regions; EstimatedBreakEvenInMonths is per RecommendationDetails row.
- When the Cost Explorer or Compute Optimizer lookup fails or is skipped,
  the response leads with a warning and additional_details holds only an error;
  base_recommendation is still valid. A lookup that runs but finds nothing
  returns empty results and no warning.
- Savings Plans recommendations carry no break-even. They return EstimatedROI (estimated savings /
  Savings Plan cost x 100 over the lookback period), which is not a payback period.
- DynamoDB reserved capacity: Cost Optimization Hub shows the payment option as PartialUpfront,
  and Cost Explorer returns the same recommendation as Heavy_Utilization. These are two names for
  one payment option, not a mismatch.

RESPONSE FORMATTING INSTRUCTIONS:
The tool may return both raw recommendation data and a formatting template.
When presenting the recommendation:
1. If a template is provided, use it to organize your response
2. If no template is provided, structure your response in a clear, logical manner
3. Always include key information like resource details, savings amounts, and implementation steps
4. Ensure all numeric values (costs, savings, metrics) are included
5. Add natural language explanations to make the information more accessible

recommendation_id.description: ID of the recommendation to retrieve details for

tools.title: Rec Details

tools.description:
Retrieves AWS Reserved Instance (RI) coverage and utilization data using the Cost Explorer API.

This tool provides insights into your Reserved Instance (RI) and Savings Plans usage patterns through two main operations:

1. get_reservation_coverage: Shows how much of your eligible usage is covered by RIs
   - Helps identify opportunities to purchase additional RIs
   - Supports grouping by dimensions like REGION, INSTANCE_TYPE, etc.
   - Can filter by specific services, regions, or instance types

2. get_reservation_utilization: Shows how effectively you're using your purchased RIs
   - Reveals underutilized or idle reserved capacity
   - Can be grouped by SUBSCRIPTION_ID to see utilization per RI
   - Helps identify RIs that could be modified or sold in the marketplace

GROUPING get_reservation_coverage (group_by):
GetReservationCoverage groups ONLY by these attributes. Keys marked "only" apply just to
that service (from the SERVICE filter, EC2 when omitted); others return a ValidationException:
- AZ: Availability Zone (e.g. us-east-1a)
- CACHE_ENGINE: ElastiCache engine (e.g. Redis, Memcached). ElastiCache and MemoryDB only
- DATABASE_ENGINE: RDS database engine (e.g. PostgreSQL, MySQL, Aurora MySQL). RDS only
- DEPLOYMENT_OPTION: deployment mode (e.g. Single-AZ, Multi-AZ). RDS only
- INSTANCE_TYPE: instance type (e.g. m4.xlarge, cache.r6g.large)
- INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY: instance family (e.g. m5, t3). EC2 only
- LINKED_ACCOUNT: member account id in the organization
- PLATFORM: operating system / platform. EC2 only
- REGION: AWS Region (e.g. us-east-1)
- TENANCY: instance tenancy. Exact, case-sensitive values: Shared, Dedicated, Host. EC2 only
SERVICE, INVOICING_ENTITY and OPERATING_SYSTEM are NOT valid group_by attributes here —
grouping coverage by them returns a ValidationException. SERVICE is a FILTER dimension instead: pass it in
`filter` (one SERVICE value per call; if you omit a SERVICE filter, Cost Explorer
defaults to EC2), and call once per service to compare across services. A filter
with more than one SERVICE value is rejected, because Cost Explorer returns each
service's figures without saying which service they belong to.
Reservation coverage applies only to reservable services. The valid SERVICE
filter values are "Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud - Compute" (the default when
omitted), "Amazon Relational Database Service", "Amazon ElastiCache",
"Amazon MemoryDB", "Amazon Redshift", "Amazon OpenSearch Service", and
"Amazon Elasticsearch Service". Use the full Cost Explorer service display name, not
"EC2"/"RDS".

GROUPING get_reservation_utilization (group_by):
GetReservationUtilization groups ONLY by SUBSCRIPTION_ID. No other attribute is
valid. The SubscriptionId it returns (and that you filter on) is a NUMERIC id
(e.g. "359809062"), not an ARN, instance id, or UUID — filtering SubscriptionId
with an ARN/UUID returns a ValidationException ("must contain only digits").

FILTER DIMENSIONS get_reservation_coverage (filter): SERVICE plus the same attributes
that service takes for group_by above (e.g. DEPLOYMENT_OPTION only with RDS); Tags and
CostCategories expressions also work. OPERATING_SYSTEM, INVOICING_ENTITY and SCOPE are
rejected for every service, as is an attribute the service does not take (e.g. TENANCY
with RDS): ValidationException "Dimension ... is not allowed". Use one SERVICE value
per call; more are rejected (see SERVICE above).

FILTER DIMENSIONS get_reservation_utilization (filter), the same for every service:
- AZ, INSTANCE_TYPE, INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY, LINKED_ACCOUNT, PLATFORM, REGION, SERVICE,
  SUBSCRIPTION_ID, TENANCY
- SCOPE: exactly "Region" (regional RI) or "Availability Zone" (zonal RI), case-sensitive;
  any other value (e.g. "region") returns no RIs and no error.
- SUBSCRIPTION_END_DATE_TIME_BEFORE, SUBSCRIPTION_END_DATE_TIME_AFTER: for expiry
  questions. Exactly one YYYY-MM-DD value each; a datetime or a second value is a
  ValidationException. BEFORE keeps RIs whose term ends before the date, AFTER those
  that end on or after it. The AFTER date must not be before start_date, and a BEFORE
  date must be later than the AFTER date (else ValidationException). Not has no effect
  on these two keys: Not(BEFORE) returns the same RIs as BEFORE. Undocumented upstream,
  so they may change.
CACHE_ENGINE, DATABASE_ENGINE, DEPLOYMENT_OPTION and OPERATING_SYSTEM are rejected here,
and so are Tags and CostCategories expressions ("Tags expression is not allowed").

SORTING (sort_by): {"Key": "<key>", "SortOrder": "DESCENDING"} (or "ASCENDING").
SortOrder is required and upper case; "descending" is a ValidationException.
get_reservation_utilization applies sort_by only with group_by; without group_by it
ignores the key (no sorting, a wrong key is not reported, and SortOrder may be omitted;
the response's sort_by_note says so), though a SortOrder other than ASCENDING or
DESCENDING is still rejected. Keys differ per operation; any other key (with group_by,
for utilization) returns "Unsupported sortKey":
- get_reservation_coverage: CoverageHoursPercentage, CoverageNormalizedUnitsPercentage,
  OnDemandCost, OnDemandHours, OnDemandNormalizedUnits, ReservedHours,
  ReservedNormalizedUnits, TotalRunningHours, TotalRunningNormalizedUnits, Time
- get_reservation_utilization: UtilizationPercentage, UtilizationPercentageInUnits,
  PurchasedHours, PurchasedUnits, TotalActualHours, TotalActualUnits, UnusedHours,
  UnusedUnits, OnDemandCostOfRIHoursUsed, NetRISavings, TotalPotentialRISavings,
  AmortizedUpfrontFee, AmortizedRecurringFee, TotalAmortizedFee, RICostForUnusedHours,
  RealizedSavings, UnrealizedSavings

FILTERING (both operations): a filter is one leaf (Dimensions; for coverage also Tags or
CostCategories), Not of one leaf, or an And of leaves and Not-leaves. Or anywhere, an And
inside an And, or a Not around anything but a leaf is a ValidationException ("Invalid
expression"). Each dimension (tags excepted) may appear only once per filter ("filtered
more than once"); put several values in one leaf instead, and they are OR'd, within the
limits above for SERVICE and the SUBSCRIPTION_END keys. MatchOptions are rejected
("MatchOptions contain not allowed match option"). Values are exact and case-sensitive:
a miscased value (e.g. "US-EAST-1", "linux/unix") returns zeros or no RIs, not an error.
The SERVICE filter defaults to Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud - Compute when omitted.

DATA FRESHNESS: Reserved Instance utilization data for the most recent 2-3 days
(counting today) is not processed yet. A get_reservation_utilization start_date inside
those days returns a DataUnavailableException, which the service sends without a
message. It means there is no data for that window, not a failure and not zero
utilization: report that, and do not resend the identical request. A start_date at
least 3 days before today is usually past that delay; query an earlier window only if
the question allows it.

RESPONSE PERIODS (both operations; dates are YYYY-MM-DD, end exclusive):
- `requested_time_period` echoes the start_date/end_date that were sent.
- get_reservation_utilization with MONTHLY granularity labels each entry's `time_period`
  with its whole calendar month (the current month's entry ends at the first day without
  data instead), but the figures cover only the requested days. A
  2026-01-24 to 2026-03-10 request returns a first entry labelled 2026-01-01 to 2026-02-01
  holding only 2026-01-24 onward, and a last entry labelled 2026-03-01 to 2026-04-01
  holding only the days before 2026-03-10. `period_note` says when this happened and the
  range the figures cover. Report those months as partial, not as whole months; `total`
  also covers only that range.
- With group_by, get_reservation_utilization returns one entry labelled with the requested
  period.
- get_reservation_coverage entries are not snapped: the first starts at the requested start
  and the last ends at the requested end.

SCOPING LARGE QUERIES: a grouped or DAILY query over a wide window or many
subscriptions can exceed the tool result size cap and return a ToolResultOversized
error. Scope such queries with `filter` (e.g. one SERVICE or one SUBSCRIPTION_ID),
a shorter window, or MONTHLY granularity before widening.

IMPORTANT: `granularity` and `group_by` are mutually exclusive. If `group_by` is
provided, `granularity` is ignored (the Cost Explorer API does not allow both for
GetReservationCoverage or GetReservationUtilization). Provide one or the other,
not both.

PAGINATION (applies only when group_by is set; an item is one group of the queried period):
- Without group_by, both operations return every time period in one response, so max_items,
  max_pages and next_token do not apply (get_reservation_utilization ignores them).
- get_reservation_coverage: max_items is the total number of groups returned. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result. Pass it, or narrow the filter, for queries that can be large.
  Top-N: sort_by + max_items=N.
- get_reservation_utilization takes max_pages (pages of 500 groups) instead of max_items, because
  its next_token only works with the same page size. Continue with next_token; if max_pages is
  omitted, the tool fetches every page, with the same 300-second limit.
- If the response has complete_dataset: false, call again with a larger max_items or max_pages,
  continue with next_token, or state in the answer that the result is partial.
- With group_by, the API's period `total` sums only the groups on its own page, so `total` is
  returned only when the whole query came back in one page. It is omitted from a multi-page,
  partial, or next_token continuation result; for the overall figure over the same window, call
  again without group_by, whose `total` covers every period.

start_date.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (inclusive). Defaults to 30 days ago if not provided.

end_date.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (exclusive). Defaults to today if not provided.

granularity.description: Time granularity of the data (DAILY or MONTHLY). Defaults to DAILY. Ignored when group_by is provided (granularity and group_by are mutually exclusive).

metrics.description: List of metrics to retrieve for coverage as a JSON string (e.g., '["Hour", "Cost"]'). Valid values are Hour, Unit and Cost; Unit is EC2 only. Defaults to Hour only.

group_by.description: Optional grouping as a JSON string. For coverage: AZ, CACHE_ENGINE, DATABASE_ENGINE, DEPLOYMENT_OPTION, INSTANCE_TYPE, INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY, LINKED_ACCOUNT, PLATFORM, REGION, or TENANCY, depending on the service (see the tool description) (SERVICE is NOT valid — filter on it instead). For utilization: SUBSCRIPTION_ID only.

filter.description: Optional filter as a JSON string (e.g., by service, region, or instance type). SERVICE defaults to EC2 when omitted; valid coverage SERVICE values are "Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud - Compute", "Amazon Relational Database Service", "Amazon ElastiCache", "Amazon MemoryDB", "Amazon Redshift", "Amazon OpenSearch Service", and "Amazon Elasticsearch Service" (use the full display name, not "EC2"/"RDS"); coverage takes one SERVICE value per call and rejects more. SubscriptionId values are numeric, not ARNs/UUIDs. A wide grouped/DAILY query may exceed the result size cap (ToolResultOversized) — scope it with a filter, a shorter window, or MONTHLY granularity.

sort_by.description: Optional sort as a JSON string: '{"Key": "<key>", "SortOrder": "DESCENDING"}'. SortOrder is required: ASCENDING or DESCENDING, upper case only. Valid keys differ per operation (see SORTING in the tool description). get_reservation_utilization ignores sort_by without group_by (the response then carries a sort_by_note).

max_items.description:
Total number of groups to return across all pages. Omit it to fetch every
page. Applies only to get_reservation_coverage with group_by set.

next_token.description:
The pagination.next_token from a previous response; continue with otherwise
identical parameters. Applies only when group_by is set.

max_pages.description:
Number of pages of 500 groups to return. Omit it to fetch every page.
Applies only to get_reservation_utilization with group_by set.

tools.name: ri-performance
tools.title: Ri Performance

tools.description:
Tool that retrieves AWS Savings Plans coverage and utilization data using the Cost Explorer API.

This tool provides insights into your Savings Plans usage patterns through three main operations:

1. get_savings_plans_coverage: Shows how much of your eligible usage is covered by Savings Plans
2. get_savings_plans_utilization: Shows overall utilization metrics for your Savings Plans
3. get_savings_plans_utilization_details: Shows detailed per-Savings Plan utilization

COVERAGE grouping and filtering (get_savings_plans_coverage):
- group_by accepts ONLY INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY, REGION, or SERVICE. LINKED_ACCOUNT is
  NOT a valid group_by attribute — grouping by it returns a ValidationException.
- filter accepts LINKED_ACCOUNT, REGION, SERVICE, INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY. To see coverage
  per member account, FILTER by one LINKED_ACCOUNT and call once per account; do
  not try to group_by LINKED_ACCOUNT. SAVINGS_PLANS_TYPE is not a coverage dimension
  (ValidationException).
- Each group_by entry is a GroupDefinition with Type and Key, e.g.
  `[{"Type": "DIMENSION", "Key": "REGION"}]`. There is no "Value" field in a
  group_by entry — a `{Key, Value}` shape is rejected (seen as a boto
  ParamValidationError typed validation_error).

DATES AND DATA FRESHNESS (all three operations):
- If `start_date` is omitted, the tool uses 30 days before today; if `end_date` is
  omitted, it uses today (exclusive, so today is not included).
- start_date must be within the last 13 months (the Cost Explorer lookback); an
  older start_date returns a ValidationException.
- Savings Plans data for the most recent 2-3 days (counting today) is not processed
  yet: yesterday is usually still missing, so excluding only today is not enough. A
  start_date inside those days returns a DataUnavailableException, which the service
  sends without a message. A window that only reaches into those days succeeds but
  silently leaves them out, so the last DAILY entry can end before end_date (MONTHLY
  labels: see RESPONSE PERIODS). A start_date at least 3 days before today is usually
  past that delay.
- A DataUnavailableException means there is no data for THIS window and filter: the
  window is too recent, no plan was active in it, or a filter value matches nothing
  (an unknown SAVINGS_PLANS_TYPE, for example, returns this error, not a
  ValidationException). Report that no data is available for that window (not zero
  utilization or coverage) and do NOT resend the identical request. Correct an unknown
  filter value; query an earlier window only if the question allows it.

UTILIZATION filters (get_savings_plans_utilization):
- filter accepts LINKED_ACCOUNT, SAVINGS_PLAN_ARN, SAVINGS_PLANS_TYPE, REGION,
  PAYMENT_OPTION, INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY. Only Dimensions, And and Not are allowed; an Or,
  Tags or CostCategories expression returns a ValidationException.

UTILIZATION DETAILS filters (get_savings_plans_utilization_details):
- filter accepts LINKED_ACCOUNT, SAVINGS_PLAN_ARN, SAVINGS_PLANS_TYPE, REGION,
  PAYMENT_OPTION, INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY, AGREEMENT_END_DATE_TIME_AFTER and
  AGREEMENT_END_DATE_TIME_BEFORE (one YYYY-MM-DD value each, compared with each plan's
  end date).
- The filter is a Cost Explorer Expression. And requires at least TWO
  operands ("And expression must have at least 2 operands"). For a single
  condition, pass the leaf object directly — e.g.
  `{"Dimensions": {"Key": "REGION", "Values": ["us-east-1"]}}` — not wrapped in
  a one-element `And`.

FILTER VALUES (exact, case-sensitive spellings):
- PAYMENT_OPTION: "No Upfront", "Partial Upfront", "All Upfront".
- SAVINGS_PLANS_TYPE (get_savings_plans_utilization and
  get_savings_plans_utilization_details; not accepted by coverage): "ComputeSavingsPlans",
  "EC2InstanceSavingsPlans", "SageMakerSavingsPlans", "DatabaseSavingsPlans".
- Any other spelling (NO_UPFRONT, Compute, COMPUTE_SP) matches nothing and returns a
  DataUnavailableException, which the service sends without a message, not a
  ValidationException. On that error with a filter set, check these spellings before
  changing the window.

SORTING (sort_by; get_savings_plans_coverage and get_savings_plans_utilization_details):
- A JSON string `{"Key": "...", "SortOrder": "ASCENDING" or "DESCENDING"}`.
- Order of operations: the API sorts every matching item by the key first, then pages;
  max_items=N keeps the first N of that sorted order. So sort_by + max_items=N returns the
  top N items by the key across everything that matches, not N arbitrary items sorted
  afterwards (see PAGINATION for what an item is).
- Coverage keys: CoveragePercentage, SpendCoveredBySavingsPlan (singular, unlike the
  metric), OnDemandCost, TotalCost, InstanceFamily, Region, Service. Sort keys are not
  dimension names: sort by InstanceFamily, group by INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY. Sorting coverage
  by InstanceFamily, Region or Service needs that dimension in group_by
  (INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY, REGION or SERVICE); otherwise the API returns a ValidationException.
- Utilization details keys: UtilizationPercentage, TotalCommitment, UsedCommitment,
  UnusedCommitment, NetSavings, AmortizedRecurringCommitment, AmortizedUpfrontCommitment.
- get_savings_plans_utilization ignores sort_by and returns its periods in date order.

RESPONSE PERIODS (all three operations):
- `requested_time_period` echoes the start_date/end_date that were sent.
- MONTHLY utilization labels each entry's TimePeriod with its whole calendar month (the
  current month's entry ends at the first day without data instead), but the figures
  cover only the requested days. A 2026-08-17 to 2026-09-10 request returns
  a first entry labelled 2026-08-01 to 2026-09-01 holding only 2026-08-17 onward, and a
  last entry labelled 2026-09-01 to 2026-10-01 holding only the days before 2026-09-10.
  `period_note` says when this happened and the range the figures cover. Report those
  months as partial, not as whole months; `total` also covers only that range.
- MONTHLY coverage entries start at the requested start; they are not snapped.
- Utilization details returns `time_period`: the requested start, and an end the API
  may move earlier to the first day without complete data. Report that period.
- `granularity` appears on coverage only when it was sent (not with group_by).

IMPORTANT: For get_savings_plans_coverage, `granularity` and `group_by` are mutually
exclusive. If `group_by` is provided, `granularity` is ignored (the Cost Explorer
GetSavingsPlansCoverage API does not allow both). Valid `group_by` dimensions for
coverage are SERVICE, REGION, or INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY. If `metrics` is omitted, coverage uses
["SpendCoveredBySavingsPlans"] (the only valid value). `granularity` does not apply to
get_savings_plans_utilization_details.

PAGINATION (get_savings_plans_coverage, where an item is one period x group entry, and
get_savings_plans_utilization_details, where an item is one Savings Plan;
get_savings_plans_utilization is not paginated and takes neither parameter):
- max_items is the total number of items returned. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result. Pass it,
  or narrow the date range or filter, for queries that can be large.
- If the response has complete_dataset: false, call again with a larger max_items, continue with
  next_token, or state in the answer that the result is partial.
- For utilization details, the API's Total covers only the Savings Plans on its own page, so
  `total` is returned only when the whole query came back in one page. It is omitted from a
  multi-page, partial, or next_token continuation result; for the overall figure over the same
  window, use the `total` of get_savings_plans_utilization. Coverage has no `total`; the
  GetSavingsPlansCoverage API does not return one.

start_date.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (inclusive). Defaults to 30 days ago if not provided. Must be within the last 13 months.

end_date.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (exclusive). Defaults to today if not provided. Savings Plans data for the last 2-3 days (counting today) is not processed yet: a start_date in those days returns a DataUnavailableException, and a window reaching into them leaves them out.

granularity.description: Time granularity of the data (DAILY or MONTHLY). Defaults to DAILY. For coverage, ignored when group_by is provided (granularity and group_by are mutually exclusive).

metrics.description: List of metrics to retrieve as a JSON string. For coverage, only 'SpendCoveredBySavingsPlans' is valid.

group_by.description: Optional grouping of results as a JSON string. For coverage, supports SERVICE, REGION, or INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY (NOT LINKED_ACCOUNT). Each entry is {"Type": ..., "Key": ...}; there is no "Value" field.

filter.description: Optional filter to apply to the results as a JSON string. Coverage filter dimensions: LINKED_ACCOUNT, REGION, SERVICE, INSTANCE_TYPE_FAMILY. And needs >=2 operands; for one condition pass the leaf object directly. Values are case-sensitive; see FILTER VALUES in the tool description.

max_items.description:
Total number of items to return across all pages. Omit it to fetch every
page. Coverage and utilization details only. With sort_by, these are the first N
items in the requested SortOrder (the top N), not N items sorted afterwards.

next_token.description:
The pagination.next_token from a previous response; continue with otherwise
identical parameters. Coverage and utilization details only.

sort_by.description:
Optional sort as a JSON string, e.g. {"Key": "CoveragePercentage", "SortOrder": "ASCENDING"}.
Applied before max_items, so sort_by + max_items=N returns the top N.
Coverage and utilization details only (ignored by get_savings_plans_utilization);
the valid keys differ per operation (see SORTING).

tools.name: sp-performance
tools.title: Sp Performance

tools.description:
Tool that describes Savings Plans inventory and purchasable offerings.

This tool provides visibility into what an account already owns and what it can buy through four
operations:

1. describe_savings_plans: the plans owned by the calling account only, with state, term, payment
   option, and expiry. No member-account plans are returned, even from a management account, so an
   empty result does not mean the organization owns none. Pass states to scope the result. For an
   organization-wide inventory use sp-performance get_savings_plans_utilization_details (one entry
   per plan ARN, and the owning account is the ARN's account field) or cost-explorer
   getDimensionValues with SAVINGS_PLAN_ARN under context=SAVINGS_PLANS. Both read Cost Explorer,
   which lists a plan only where it has utilization records in the window, so pass an explicit
   12-month start_date and end_date: a shorter window drops retired and idle plans, and a member
   account's idle plan still displaces a new purchase.
2. describe_savings_plan_rates: The rates on one Savings Plan the customer already owns.
3. describe_savings_plans_offerings: The offerings available to purchase.
4. describe_savings_plans_offering_rates: The rates for offerings available to purchase.

USE THIS TOOL FOR:
- **What plans the calling account owns** — including plans in the queued, returned, and
  payment-failed states, which Cost Explorer does not report on
- **When a plan expires or can still be returned** — the end and returnableUntil fields
- **The rates locked in on an existing plan**
- **What is available to purchase and at what rate** — to compare the rate one plan type, term, and
  payment option gets against another for the same usage

DO NOT USE THIS TOOL FOR:
- Coverage or utilization of existing plans, which is sp-performance
- Recommended savings plans to purchase, which is sp-recommendation

Tags come back on each plan in describe_savings_plans, so there is no separate tag operation.

IMPORTANT: the vocabulary here differs from Cost Explorer's, so values carried over from a Cost
Explorer response or recommendation will be rejected. See the individual parameter descriptions.

PAGINATION (all four operations):
- max_items is the total number of items returned. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result. Pass it,
  or narrow the filters, for queries that can be large (an unfiltered offering or offering-rate
  query runs to thousands of entries).
- If the response has complete_dataset: false, call again with a larger max_items, continue with
  next_token, or state in the answer that the result is partial.

A large result from any of these operations is automatically offloaded to session SQL to save
tokens: the response carries data_stored=True and a table_name (one row per plan, rate, or
offering) instead of the inline list, and the rows are queried with the session-sql tool. A small
result is returned inline unchanged.

savings_plan_arns.description: The Savings Plan ARNs to describe as a list.

savings_plan_ids.description: The Savings Plan IDs to describe as a list.

states.description:
The current states of the Savings Plans as a list. One or more of
payment-pending, payment-failed, active, retired, queued, queued-deleted,
pending-return, and returned. Omitting it returns every state, which for a mature
account means mostly retired plans.

savings_plan_id.description:
The ID of the Savings Plan to describe rates for. Required for
describe_savings_plan_rates.

offering_ids.description:
The IDs of the offerings as a list. Used by both offering
operations.

payment_options.description:
The payment options as a list. One or more of 'No Upfront',
'Partial Upfront', and 'All Upfront' — note the spaces. Used by both offering
operations.

plan_types.description:
The plan types as a list. One or more of Compute, EC2Instance,
SageMaker, and Database. Used by both offering operations.

product_type.description:
The product type — EC2, Fargate, Lambda, SageMaker, RDS, DSQL, DynamoDB,
ElastiCache, DocDB, Neptune, Timestream, Keyspaces, DMS, or OpenSearch. Used by
describe_savings_plans_offerings.

products.description:
The products as a list, from the same set as product_type. Used by
describe_savings_plans_offering_rates.

durations.description:
The durations, in seconds as a list. A one-year term is 31536000
and a three-year term is 94608000.

currencies.description: The currencies as a list. One or more of CNY, USD, and EUR.

service_codes.description:
The service codes as a list. describe_savings_plans_offerings takes
the plan's own code: ComputeSavingsPlans (Compute and EC2Instance plans),
MachineLearningSavingsPlans (SageMaker plans), or DatabaseSavingsPlans (Database
plans), as in the serviceCode field of a returned offering. Any other value,
including a rate code such as AmazonSageMaker, matches nothing and returns an empty
result, not an error. The exception is a value containing EC2 in upper or lower
case, such as AmazonEC2, ec2 or EC2InstanceSavingsPlans: it fails the whole request,
even alongside a valid code, with a ValidationException whose message lists
AmazonEC2 as allowed. For EC2Instance plans use ComputeSavingsPlans.
describe_savings_plans_offering_rates takes the code of the service the rate
applies to: AmazonEC2, AmazonECS, AmazonEKS, AWSLambda, AmazonSageMaker, AmazonRDS,
AuroraDSQL, AmazonDynamoDB, AmazonElastiCache, AmazonDocDB, AmazonNeptune,
AmazonTimestream, AmazonMCS, AWSDatabaseMigrationSvc, and AmazonES.

usage_types.description:
The usage types as a list. The two offering operations use different
usage types, and a value from one matches nothing on the other. An offering's usage
type names the plan, such as ComputeSP:1yrNoUpfront, or EC2SP:m5.1yrNoUpfront for a
regional plan. A rate's usage type names the usage it covers, such as
BoxUsage:m5.large.
Outside us-east-1 a regional usage type carries a region prefix
(AFS1-EC2SP:c5.1yrAllUpfront, USW2-BoxUsage:m5.large). In us-east-1 most have none,
but some rates carry one (USE1-Fargate-GB-Hours). A value that matches nothing
returns an empty result, not an error, so copy values from the usageType field of
a returned offering or rate.

filters.description:
The filters as a list of {"name": ..., "values": [...]} objects. The
accepted names differ per operation: describe_savings_plans takes region,
ec2-instance-family, commitment, upfront, term, savings-plan-type, payment-option,
start, end, and instance-family; describe_savings_plan_rates takes region, instanceType,
productDescription, tenancy, productType, serviceCode, usageType, and operation;
describe_savings_plans_offerings takes region and instanceFamily; and
describe_savings_plans_offering_rates takes region, instanceFamily, instanceType,
productDescription, and tenancy. For describe_savings_plans the values are strings, numbers included, matched exactly and case-sensitively, and a value that
matches no plan returns an empty list, not an error: savings-plan-type is Compute,
EC2Instance, SageMaker, or Database; payment-option is 'All Upfront', 'Partial
Upfront', or 'No Upfront', with the spaces; term is the duration in seconds as a
string, "31536000" or "94608000"; upfront and commitment are decimal strings such as
"4.38", with no currency sign; start and end are exact timestamps such as
"2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", matched to the millisecond rather than as a range; region
is a region code such as us-east-1; and ec2-instance-family and instance-family are an
instance family such as m5. The two rate operations use the pricing vocabulary, not
Cost Explorer's, and a value in another spelling also returns an empty list: tenancy
is lower case, shared or dedicated (Cost Explorer's Shared matches nothing); and
productDescription is the full operating system name such as Linux/UNIX, Windows, or
Red Hat Enterprise Linux (Linux alone matches nothing).

max_items.description:
Total number of items to return across all pages. Omit it to fetch every
page.

next_token.description:
The pagination.next_token from a previous response; continue with otherwise
identical parameters.

tools.name: sp-explorer
tools.title: Sp Explorer

tools.description:
Tool that retrieves AWS Savings Plans purchase recommendations using the Cost Explorer API.

This tool provides the commitment a customer should consider buying, and the evidence behind it,
through four operations:

1. get_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation: The recommended commitment for a given plan type,
   term, and payment option, with estimated savings, coverage, and utilization.
2. get_savings_plan_purchase_recommendation_details: The hourly data-points behind a single
   recommendation, keyed by the RecommendationDetailId returned above.
3. start_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation_generation: Recalculates the recommendation against
   the latest usage and the current Savings Plans inventory.
4. list_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation_generation: Generation history with status and
   timestamps.

USE THIS TOOL FOR:
- **What to buy** — the recommended commitment for a given plan type, term, and payment option
- **Whether that commitment would go unused** — the hourly EstimatedNewCommitmentUtilization behind
  the recommendation, rather than a figure derived from the raw spend series
- **How stale the recommendation is** — when it was last generated
- **A recommendation that reflects a purchase just made** — refresh it, since the stored one predates
  the purchase

DO NOT USE THIS TOOL FOR:
- What the customer already owns, which is sp-explorer
- Coverage or utilization of existing plans, which is sp-performance
- Modeling a commitment the customer specifies rather than a recommended one, which is
  sp-purchase-analyzer

ASYNCHRONOUS: start_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation_generation returns a RecommendationId and
an EstimatedCompletionTime, not a recommendation. Poll
list_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation_generation, filtered on that RecommendationId, until
GenerationStatus leaves PROCESSING, then read the refreshed recommendation with
get_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation. Completion time scales with the size of the billing
family, so read EstimatedCompletionTime rather than assuming a duration.

WRITE OPERATION: a consolidated billing family can refresh recommendations three times a day, and
only one generation runs at a time. Check the generation history before starting another — a
recommendation generated hours ago is usually fresh enough, and a refresh that fails leaves the
older recommendation in place with a timestamp that does not say so.

IMPORTANT: get_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation requires savings_plans_type, term_in_years,
payment_option, and lookback_period_in_days. None of them has a default — each changes the
recommended commitment, so the caller must choose. Recommendations are precomputed and may be
stale; the response carries the generation timestamp. DATABASE_SP is sold only as ONE_YEAR with
NO_UPFRONT. An empty recommendation (an unsold combination, or no eligible usage) comes with a
message and does not mean potential savings are zero.

PAGINATION (get_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation, where the items are the recommendation
details, and list_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation_generation; the other operations take
neither parameter):
- max_items is the total number of items returned. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result. Pass it,
  or narrow the filter, for queries that can be large.
- If the response has complete_dataset: false, call again with a larger max_items, continue with
  next_token, or state in the answer that the result is partial.

savings_plans_type.description:
COMPUTE_SP, EC2_INSTANCE_SP, SAGEMAKER_SP, or DATABASE_SP. Required for get_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation.
DATABASE_SP is sold only as ONE_YEAR with NO_UPFRONT; any other term or payment option
returns no recommendation, which does not mean there is nothing to buy.

payment_option.description:
NO_UPFRONT, PARTIAL_UPFRONT, or ALL_UPFRONT. Required for get_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation. The API shape also accepts three
LIGHT/MEDIUM/HEAVY_UTILIZATION values, which are Reserved Instance utilization levels and do not apply to Savings Plans.

lookback_period_in_days.description: SEVEN_DAYS, THIRTY_DAYS, or SIXTY_DAYS. Required for get_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation.

filter.description:
Filter recommendations by Account ID: a Dimensions expression with Key
LINKED_ACCOUNT and Values one or more Account IDs, optionally wrapped in a single Not to
exclude those accounts, for example
{"Not": {"Dimensions": {"Key": "LINKED_ACCOUNT", "Values": ["111122223333"]}}}.
MatchOptions, if given, must be EQUALS. And, Or, and a Not inside another Not are not
supported. Applies to get_savings_plans_purchase_recommendation only.

recommendation_detail_id.description: Required for get_savings_plan_purchase_recommendation_details. Comes from the RecommendationDetailId field of a recommendation.

max_items.description:
Total number of items (recommendation details, or generations) to return
across all pages. Omit it to fetch every page. Paginated operations only.

next_token.description:
The pagination.next_token from a previous response; continue with otherwise
identical parameters. A token belongs to the request that produced it and to the
recommendation it was generated against, so it stops working once the parameters
change or the recommendation is regenerated; read from the first page again when that
happens. Paginated operations only.

tools.name: sp-recommendation
tools.title: Sp Recommendation

tools.description:
Tool that runs AWS Savings Plans Purchase Analyzer what-if analyses using the Cost Explorer API.

This tool estimates the cost, coverage, and utilization impact of a commitment purchase the caller
specifies, through three operations:

1. start_commitment_purchase_analysis: Starts an analysis. Returns an AnalysisId and an
   EstimatedCompletionTime; it does not return results.
2. get_commitment_purchase_analysis: Retrieves a result by AnalysisId.
3. list_commitment_purchase_analyses: Lists the analyses for the account.

USE THIS TOOL FOR:
- **What commitment reaches a specific coverage target** — TARGET_AVERAGE_COVERAGE
- **What a specific commitment would do** — CUSTOM_COMMITMENT
- **What the largest saving would be, modelled now** — MAX_SAVINGS
- **What an expiring plan is worth** — exclude it and compare the result
- **Retrieving an analysis that was already started** — by its AnalysisId

DO NOT USE THIS TOOL FOR:
- A precomputed recommendation, which is sp-recommendation
- What the customer already owns, which is sp-explorer
- Coverage or utilization of existing plans, which is sp-performance

ASYNCHRONOUS: start_commitment_purchase_analysis returns an AnalysisId and an
EstimatedCompletionTime, not a result. Report the AnalysisId before waiting on it — a wait that ends
early leaves the analysis running server-side, and recovering it then means listing the account's
analyses and picking one out by start time. Then poll get_commitment_purchase_analysis until
AnalysisStatus leaves PROCESSING. Completion time scales with account size, so read
EstimatedCompletionTime rather than assuming a duration.

WRITE OPERATION: an account can start 20 analyses a day, one at a time. GenerationExistsException
means one is already running, ServiceQuotaExceededException means the day's 20 are used up, and
LimitExceededException is transient. They are not interchangeable.

IMPORTANT: the API takes one nested CommitmentPurchaseAnalysisConfiguration, which this tool builds
from analysis_type, savings_plans_to_add, look_back_start, and look_back_end. All four are needed —
savings_plans_to_add for every analysis type, MAX_SAVINGS included, since the plan type, term, and
payment option live inside it. None has a default: each changes the result, and a wrong guess spends
one of the day's analyses on a scenario nobody asked for. A validation error names the nested field
it rejected rather than the parameter, so read the path in the message. An analysis also carries the
configuration it was run with, so read AnalysisType from a result rather than assuming which
scenario it modelled.

PAGINATION (list_commitment_purchase_analyses only; the other operations take neither parameter):
- max_items is the total number of analyses returned. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result.
- If the response has complete_dataset: false, call again with a larger max_items, continue with
  next_token, or state in the answer that the result is partial.

analysis_type.description:
The type of analysis — MAX_SAVINGS, CUSTOM_COMMITMENT, or
TARGET_AVERAGE_COVERAGE. Required for start_commitment_purchase_analysis.

savings_plans_to_add.description:
Savings Plans to include in the analysis. Each entry accepts
SavingsPlansType (COMPUTE_SP, EC2_INSTANCE_SP, SAGEMAKER_SP, or DATABASE_SP),
TermInYears (ONE_YEAR or THREE_YEARS), PaymentOption (NO_UPFRONT, PARTIAL_UPFRONT, or
ALL_UPFRONT), SavingsPlansCommitment as an hourly amount, Region, InstanceFamily, and
OfferingId. Required for start_commitment_purchase_analysis — for example
[{"SavingsPlansType": "COMPUTE_SP", "TermInYears": "ONE_YEAR", "PaymentOption":
"NO_UPFRONT"}].

savings_plans_to_exclude.description:
Savings Plan ARNs to exclude from the analysis. Use it to model the
gap an expiring plan leaves behind.

look_back_start.description:
Start of the time period associated with the analysis, in YYYY-MM-DD format.
Required for start_commitment_purchase_analysis.

look_back_end.description:
End of the time period associated with the analysis, in YYYY-MM-DD format.
Required for start_commitment_purchase_analysis.

savings_plans_target_coverage.description:
The target Savings Plans coverage as a whole-number
percentage from 10 to 100 — 85, not 0.85 or 85.5. It defines the target average hourly
coverage that the recommended Savings Plans commitment should achieve over the lookback
period. Required when analysis_type is TARGET_AVERAGE_COVERAGE.

account_scope.description: The account scope that you want your analysis for — PAYER or LINKED.

account_id.description: The account that the analysis is for.

analysis_id.description:
The analysis ID that's associated with the commitment purchase analysis.
Required for get_commitment_purchase_analysis.

tools.description:
Execute SQL queries on the persistent session database.

This tool queries tables created by other tools (like cost_explorer_sql) within the current session.
All tools share the same database, allowing cross-tool data analysis and joins.

Use this tool to:
- Query tables created by cost_explorer_sql and other tools
- Join data from multiple AWS APIs
- Perform complex analysis across different data sources

Adding data: pass `schema` (column definitions, e.g. ["service TEXT", "cost REAL"]) and `data`
(rows) to create a table before `query` runs. If `table_name` is omitted while `schema` and
`data` are given, the tool creates a table named `user_data_<random 8 hex>`.

Common queries:
- SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' -- List all tables
- SELECT * FROM [table_name] LIMIT 10 -- Preview table data

schema.description: Optional column definitions for user data (e.g. ["service TEXT", "cost REAL"])

data.description: Optional array of data rows to add to database before querying

tools.description:
Retrieves a list of billing groups from AWS Billing Conductor.

This tool retrieve billing groups for a given billing period.
If no billing period is provided, the current billing period is used.
A billing_period after the current month (UTC) is a projection, not a record: the response sets
`billing_period_is_future: true` and lists what is recorded today as in effect that month.

The tool returns information about:
- Billing group ARN, name, and description
- Billing group type (STANDARD or TRANSFER_BILLING)
- Billing group status (ACTIVE, PRIMARY_ACCOUNT_MISSING, or PENDING)
- Primary account ID
- Computation preference (pricing plan ARN)
- Account grouping settings (auto-associate, responsibility transfer ARN)
- Group size (number of member accounts)
- Creation and last modified timestamps

You can filter billing groups by:
- ARNs: Filter by specific billing group ARNs
- Names: exactly one name search, a case-sensitive prefix match:
  [{"SearchOption": "STARTS_WITH", "SearchValue": "<prefix>"}]
- Statuses: at most 2 of ACTIVE, PRIMARY_ACCOUNT_MISSING, PENDING (omit it for every status)
- Billing group types: Filter by type (STANDARD, TRANSFER_BILLING)
- Primary account IDs: Filter by primary account ID
- PricingPlan: a full pricing plan ARN (arn:aws:billingconductor::<account>:pricingplan/<id>),
  not a bare ID
- Auto-associate: Filter by auto-associate setting
- Responsibility transfer ARNs: Filter by responsibility transfer ARNs

Pagination: `max_items` is the total number of items to return. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result; pass it, or narrow the filters, when the result can be large. A partial result leads
with `complete_dataset: false` and a `warning`: call again with a larger `max_items`, continue by
passing `pagination.next_token` back as `next_token`, or say in the answer that the result is
partial. `pagination.items_returned` counts the items in this response, not every item that exists.

Example 1: {"billing_period": "2025-01"}
Example 2 (with filter): {"filters": "{"Statuses": ["ACTIVE"], "BillingGroupTypes": ["STANDARD"]}", "billing_period": "2025-01"}

If not provided, the current billing period is used.

filters.description:

- Arns: List of billing group ARNs to retrieve
- Names: Exactly one name search object with SearchOption "STARTS_WITH" and

- Statuses: Up to 2 of "ACTIVE", "PRIMARY_ACCOUNT_MISSING", "PENDING"
- BillingGroupTypes: List of types ("STANDARD", "TRANSFER_BILLING")
- PrimaryAccountIds: List of primary account IDs

tools.description:
Retrieves a summary report of actual AWS charges and calculated AWS charges
based on the associated pricing plan of a billing group.

This tool retrieve cost reports for billing groups.
If no billing period is provided, the current billing period is used.
A billing_period after the current month (UTC) fails with validation_error before any AWS call;
the service would return $0 for every billing group.
A past month with no billing group in effect returns an empty list, not an error.

The tool returns cost report information for each billing group:
- Billing group ARN
- AWS cost (actual AWS charges)
- Proforma cost (hypothetical charges based on the associated pricing plan)
- Margin (proforma cost minus AWS cost; negative means the proforma cost is below the AWS cost)
- Margin percentage (margin divided by AWS cost, as a fraction, not a percent: -0.25 means -25%;
  "0.0" when the AWS cost is 0)
- Currency (displayed currency)
- `decimal_values` (aws_cost, proforma_cost, margin and margin_percentage, digit for digit, as
  strings in plain decimal notation)
- MONETARY AMOUNTS ARE STRINGS. They can come in exponent form ("5.0E-7") and with floating-point
  rounding digits ("-12.340000000000003"). `decimal_values` removes the exponent but keeps every
  digit; parse them as decimals, never floats, and round only for display.

You can filter cost reports by:
- BillingGroupArns: Filter by specific billing group ARNs (1 to 100 ARNs)

Pagination: `max_items` is the total number of items to return. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result; pass it, or narrow the filters, when the result can be large. A partial result leads
with `complete_dataset: false` and a `warning`: call again with a larger `max_items`, continue by
passing `pagination.next_token` back as `next_token`, or say in the answer that the result is
partial. `pagination.items_returned` counts the items in this response, not every item that exists.

Example 1: {"billing_period": "2025-01"}
Example 2 (with filter): {"filters": "{"BillingGroupArns": ["arn:aws:billingconductor::123456789012:billinggroup/abc"]}", "billing_period": "2025-01"}

billing_period.description:
Optional billing period in YYYY-MM format (e.g., "2025-01").
If not provided, the current billing period is used.
A month after the current month (UTC) fails with validation_error.

filters.description:

- BillingGroupArns: List of billing group ARNs (minimum 1, maximum 100)

tools.description:
Retrieves the margin summary report for a specific billing group, which includes
the AWS cost and charged amount (pro forma cost) broken down by attributes such as AWS service
name or billing period.

This tool retrieve detailed cost reports for a
single billing group, optionally broken down by product name and/or billing period.
A BillingPeriodRange whose InclusiveStartBillingPeriod is after the current month (UTC) fails
with validation_error before any AWS call; the service would return no results.
A range with no data for the billing group (for example, months before it took effect) returns
no results, not an error.

The tool returns margin summary report results for the billing group:
- Billing group ARN
- Attributes (key-value pairs for grouping, e.g., PRODUCT_NAME: "S3", BILLING_PERIOD: "2025-01")
- AWS cost (actual AWS charges)
- Proforma cost (hypothetical charges based on the associated pricing plan)
- Margin (proforma cost minus AWS cost; negative means the proforma cost is below the AWS cost)
- Margin percentage (margin divided by AWS cost, as a fraction, not a percent: -0.25 means -25%;
  "0.0" when the AWS cost is 0)
- Currency (displayed currency)
- `decimal_values` (aws_cost, proforma_cost, margin and margin_percentage, digit for digit, as
  strings in plain decimal notation)
- MONETARY AMOUNTS ARE STRINGS. They can come in exponent form ("5.0E-7") and with floating-point
  rounding digits ("-12.340000000000003"). `decimal_values` removes the exponent but keeps every
  digit; parse them as decimals, never floats, and round only for display.

You can customize the report by:
- BillingPeriodRange: JSON string {"InclusiveStartBillingPeriod": "YYYY-MM",
  "ExclusiveEndBillingPeriod": "YYYY-MM"}, up to 12 months. The end month is excluded:
  2025-01 to 2025-04 covers January to March. Without it, the report covers only the current
  month, month-to-date (still changing).
- GroupBy: JSON array string with values "PRODUCT_NAME" and/or "BILLING_PERIOD". Without
  BILLING_PERIOD, the months of a range are summed: no GroupBy gives one row for the whole
  range, PRODUCT_NAME alone one row per product. Include BILLING_PERIOD in GroupBy to get one
  row per month.

Pagination: `max_items` is the total number of items to return. If it is omitted, the tool fetches every page for up to 300 seconds (BCM_MCP_PAGINATION_MAX_SECONDS), then returns a partial result; pass it, or narrow the filters, when the result can be large. A partial result leads
with `complete_dataset: false` and a `warning`: call again with a larger `max_items`, continue by
passing `pagination.next_token` back as `next_token`, or say in the answer that the result is
partial. `pagination.items_returned` counts the items in this response, not every item that exists.
Results come in pages of up to 300; the service returns at least 200 per page, so a `max_items`
below 200 can return up to 200.
The next_token expires shortly after the first call; after that, call again without next_token.

Example 1: {"arn": "arn:aws:billingconductor::123456789012:billinggroup/abc", "group_by": "["PRODUCT_NAME"]"}
Example 2: {"arn": "arn:aws:billingconductor::123456789012:billinggroup/abc", "group_by": "["PRODUCT_NAME", "BILLING_PERIOD"]", "billing_period_range": "{"InclusiveStartBillingPeriod": "2025-01", "ExclusiveEndBillingPeriod": "2025-07"}"}

arn.description: The ARN that uniquely identifies the billing group.

billing_period_range.description:
Optional JSON string with InclusiveStartBillingPeriod and
ExclusiveEndBillingPeriod (YYYY-MM, end month excluded, up to 12 months). Omitted:
the current month, month-to-date.

group_by.description:
Optional JSON string with attributes to group by ("PRODUCT_NAME", "BILLING_PERIOD").
Include "BILLING_PERIOD" for one row per month; without it a multi-month range is summed.

max_items.description:
Optional total number of items to return. Omit it to fetch every page.
A max_items below 200 can return up to 200, the service's smallest page.

next_token.description: Optional pagination token from a previous response.

tools.name: list-pricing-plans-for-rule
